offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first/second); Class 6 Felony (third); Class 5 Felony (fourth); Class 4 Felony (fifth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or any substance that impairs driving ability
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
enhancements: BAC .17 or higher (mandatory chemical dependency evaluation)
notes: Implied consent under SDCL § 32-23-10. Refusal to submit to testing results in automatic license revocation. 30-day minimum license revocation for first offense.

elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions
enhancements: BAC .17 or higher (mandatory chemical dependency evaluation)
notes: Court may order alcohol treatment program. Eligible for restricted license after 30 days.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (second); Class 6 Felony (third); Class 5 Felony (fourth); Class 4 Felony (fifth+)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 1-year license revocation (third); 2-year license revocation (fourth); 3-year license revocation (fifth+)
notes: Third offense is a Class 6 Felony. Fourth is Class 5. Fifth and subsequent are Class 4 Felonies. 24/7 sobriety program may be ordered.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of a controlled drug or substance
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any controlled substance
To a degree that renders the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
Ingestion of marijuana or any controlled substance listed in SDCL § 34-20B
notes: Any amount of a controlled substance in blood is sufficient for a charge. Includes prescription medications that impair driving.

elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. May result in license suspension.

statute_title: Leaving Scene of Accident Involving Injury or Death
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render reasonable assistance
notes: Property-damage-only hit-and-run under SDCL § 32-34-6 is a Class 2 Misdemeanor. Duty to stop, identify, and render aid.

elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: Vehicular homicide while intoxicated is a Class 3 Felony. May also be charged as second-degree manslaughter under SDCL § 22-16-20.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: South Dakota does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths charged as second-degree manslaughter or vehicular homicide (SDCL § 22-16-41) depending on circumstances.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public highway
Defendant's license was suspended or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Additional period of suspension may be added. DUI-related suspensions carry stricter penalties.

offense_class: Class 6 Felony; Class 5 Felony if creating substantial risk of injury or death
elements: Defendant was operating a motor vehicle
A law enforcement officer signaled the defendant to stop
Defendant willfully failed to stop or fled
Defendant knew or should have known the person signaling was a law enforcement officer
enhancements: Creating substantial risk of serious injury or death to any person (Class 5 Felony)
notes: Enhanced if flight creates risk of serious injury. License revocation may be imposed.

statute_title: Unauthorized Possession of Controlled Drug or Substance
offense_class: Class 5 Felony (Schedule I/II); Class 6 Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled drug or substance
The substance was listed in the schedules of controlled substances
Defendant did not have a valid prescription or authorization
enhancements: Possession within 1,000 feet of a school, park, or public housing (SDCL § 22-42-19)
notes: South Dakota has strict drug laws. Possession of any amount of Schedule I/II substances is a felony.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (2 oz or less); Class 6 Felony (2 oz to 1/2 lb); Class 5 Felony (1/2 lb to 1 lb); Class 4 Felony (1 lb to 10 lbs)
penalty_max: 1 year (2 oz or less); 2 years (2 oz to 1/2 lb); 5 years (1/2 lb to 1 lb); 10 years (1 lb to 10 lbs)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed marijuana
The amount possessed determines the classification
notes: South Dakota voters approved recreational marijuana in 2020 but the measure was struck down by the state Supreme Court. Marijuana remains illegal. Medical marijuana program enacted in 2020.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Defendant did not have lawful authorization
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II. Any amount of possession is a felony. Larger amounts may support distribution charges.

elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Defendant did not have lawful authorization
notes: Meth is the most commonly prosecuted drug in South Dakota. Any amount is a felony.

statute_title: Distribution of Controlled Drug or Substance
offense_class: Class 4 Felony (first); Class 3 Felony (second); Class 2 Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant distributed, dispensed, or manufactured a controlled substance
Or possessed with intent to distribute
The substance was a controlled drug or substance
notes: Distribution to a minor under 18 by a person over 18 is a Class 2 Felony. Enhanced penalties near schools.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (1 oz to 1/2 lb); Class 3 Felony (1/2 lb to 1 lb); Class 2 Felony (1 lb+)
elements: Defendant distributed or dispensed marijuana
Or possessed marijuana with intent to distribute
notes: Separate penalties apply for marijuana distribution based on weight thresholds.

statute_title: Manufacture of Controlled Drug or Substance
elements: Defendant manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
The substance was listed in the schedules of controlled substances
enhancements: Manufacturing meth in the presence of a minor (SDCL § 22-42-18)
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine or any controlled substance carries the same distribution penalties. Additional child endangerment charges if minors present.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With the intent to use it to ingest, inhale, or introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Distribution of paraphernalia is a Class 1 Misdemeanor. Distribution to a minor is a Class 6 Felony.

elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to distribute or dispense
Intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, or other circumstances
notes: Intent to distribute is typically inferred from large quantities, packaging materials, scales, large amounts of cash, or other indicative evidence.

offense_class: Class A Felony (death eligible); Class B Felony (mandatory life without parole if death not sought)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
With premeditated design to effect the death
Or during the perpetration of certain enumerated felonies (felony murder)
enhancements: Murder during commission of a felony (felony murder)
notes: South Dakota retains the death penalty. Class A Felony if death penalty sought. Life without parole is the mandatory minimum.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Without premeditation but with intent to kill
Or with a depraved mind regardless of human life
notes: Second-degree murder covers intentional killings without premeditation and depraved-heart killings.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Without a design to effect death
In a heat of passion or upon sudden quarrel
But in a cruel or unusual manner
notes: First-degree manslaughter in South Dakota corresponds to voluntary manslaughter in other states. Heat of passion is the typical basis.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
Without any design to effect death
By criminal negligence or reckless conduct
notes: Second-degree manslaughter corresponds to involuntary manslaughter. Covers unintentional killings resulting from criminal negligence.

elements: Defendant attempted to cause or caused serious bodily injury to another
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the value of human life
Or with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Aggravated assault is a Class 3 Felony. Serious bodily injury means injury creating a substantial risk of death.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor; Class 6 Felony (third or subsequent offense within 5 years)
elements: Defendant attempted to cause bodily injury to another
Or recklessly caused bodily injury to another
Or negligently caused bodily injury with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Third or subsequent conviction within 5 years (Class 6 Felony)
notes: First and second offenses are Class 1 Misdemeanors. Third or subsequent within 5 years becomes a Class 6 Felony.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused bodily injury to another person
Without legal justification
notes: South Dakota combines assault and battery under the simple assault statute. No separate battery offense.

elements: Defendant took personal property from the person or presence of another
Against the victim's will
By force, intimidation, or threat of force
While armed with a dangerous weapon or inflicting serious bodily injury
notes: First-degree robbery requires being armed with a dangerous weapon or inflicting serious bodily injury. Second-degree robbery (SDCL § 22-30-6) is a Class 4 Felony.

statute_title: Robbery in the First Degree — Armed
elements: Defendant took personal property from the person or presence of another
Against the victim's will
By force or intimidation
While armed with a dangerous weapon
notes: Armed robbery falls under first-degree robbery in South Dakota. The dangerous weapon element elevates second-degree to first-degree.

offense_class: Class C Felony; Class 1 Felony if victim suffers serious injury
elements: Defendant seized, confined, or carried away another person
Without lawful authority
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield, commit a felony, inflict injury, or terrorize
enhancements: Victim suffers serious bodily injury (Class 1 Felony)
notes: Kidnapping in the first degree (SDCL § 22-19-1) carries up to life imprisonment. Second-degree kidnapping (SDCL § 22-19-1.1) is a Class 3 Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly set fire to or burned any structure or property
Where there was a reasonable expectation that a human being was present
enhancements: Death or serious bodily injury resulting
notes: First-degree arson involves occupied structures. Second-degree arson (SDCL § 22-33-2) involves unoccupied structures and is a Class 4 Felony. Third-degree arson (SDCL § 22-33-3) is a Class 6 Felony.

offense_class: One class below the completed offense
penalty_max: Life imprisonment (attempted first-degree murder); varies by degree
elements: Defendant intended to commit murder
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The victim survived
notes: Attempted first-degree murder is a Class B Felony. Attempted second-degree murder is a Class C Felony.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
elements: Defendant attempted to cause serious bodily injury to another
With a dangerous weapon
Or caused serious bodily injury under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Falls under the aggravated assault statute. A dangerous weapon includes firearms, knives, and any instrument capable of causing death or serious bodily harm.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (under $400); Class 1 Misdemeanor ($400-$1,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,500); Class 5 Felony ($2,500-$5,000); Class 4 Felony ($5,000-$100,000); Class 3 Felony ($100,000+)
penalty_max: 30 days to 15 years depending on value
elements: Defendant took or exercised unauthorized control over property of another
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: South Dakota consolidates larceny, embezzlement, and obtaining by false pretenses under a unified theft statute. Thresholds determine felony vs. misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property exceeded $5,000
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Grand theft is theft of property valued at $5,000 or more. Includes theft of livestock.

elements: Defendant took property of another
The value of the property was under $1,000
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Prior theft convictions may elevate charge
notes: Petty theft covers thefts under $1,000 in value.

elements: Defendant concealed upon their person or in a container, unpurchased merchandise
From a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise without paying
notes: Penalties follow the same value thresholds as general theft. Merchants may also pursue civil penalties.

elements: Defendant entered or remained in an occupied structure
With intent to commit any crime therein
While armed with a dangerous weapon or while inflicting or attempting to inflict bodily injury
notes: First-degree burglary requires an occupied structure plus an aggravating factor. Second-degree burglary (SDCL § 22-32-3) is a Class 3 Felony. Third-degree burglary (SDCL § 22-32-8) is a Class 4 Felony.

statute_title: Burglary in the First Degree — Occupied Dwelling
elements: Defendant entered or remained in an occupied dwelling
With intent to commit any crime therein
While armed or while inflicting bodily injury
notes: Occupied dwelling burglary is the most serious form. Unoccupied dwelling burglary falls under second-degree.

elements: Defendant took or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle
Belonging to another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Most vehicles exceed the $5,000 felony threshold.

offense_class: Same classification as theft based on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Penalties mirror theft classifications based on the value of the stolen property.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,500); Class 5 Felony ($2,500-$5,000); Class 4 Felony ($5,000+)
penalty_max: 1 year to 10 years depending on damage amount
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged or destroyed property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Restitution is typically ordered in addition to criminal penalties.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (first); Class 1 Misdemeanor (second or subsequent)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained on property of another
Without authorization
After being notified to leave or stay off
notes: Notice may be given verbally, in writing, or by conspicuous posting of signs.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (under $1,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000-$2,500); higher for greater amounts
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
The amount of damage determines the classification
notes: South Dakota uses the intentional damage to property statute rather than a separate criminal mischief statute.

statute_title: Domestic Abuse — Violation of Protection Order
elements: Defendant committed physical harm, bodily injury, or attempted bodily injury against a household member
Or violated a domestic protection order
notes: Domestic abuse is charged under the applicable assault statute with domestic enhancement. Protection order violations are separately charged under SDCL § 25-10-13.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused bodily injury to a household member or former household member
Or attempted to cause bodily injury to a household member
notes: Domestic battery is prosecuted under the simple assault statute with the domestic relationship as context. Batterer's treatment program may be ordered.

elements: Defendant abused, exposed, tortured, or cruelly punished a minor child
Or neglected a child in a manner that caused harm or risk of harm
notes: Mandatory reporting requirements apply. Child endangerment through DUI may be charged separately.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony (serious bodily injury); Class 4 Felony (other abuse)
elements: Defendant intentionally abused a minor child
Causing bodily injury or serious bodily injury
Or creating a substantial risk of harm
notes: Child abuse resulting in death may be charged as manslaughter or murder.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first); Class 6 Felony (subsequent within 10 years)
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated the terms of the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 10 years (Class 6 Felony)
notes: Includes domestic abuse protection orders, stalking protection orders, and no-contact orders.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first); Class 6 Felony (second or subsequent within 10 years)
elements: Defendant willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly followed or harassed another person
Making a credible threat with intent to place the victim in reasonable fear
enhancements: Violation of a stalking protection order
notes: Includes in-person and electronic/cyber stalking. Protection orders available to victims.

elements: Defendant engaged in a pattern of conduct directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, threatened, or harassed
notes: Harassment can be a predicate for stalking charges if it escalates to repeated conduct with credible threats.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of Elder or Adult with Disability
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a person aged 65 or older or an adult with a disability
The conduct caused harm or risk of harm
Or the defendant financially exploited the victim
notes: Mandatory reporting requirements apply for suspected elder abuse.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon Without a Permit
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon on or about their person
Without a valid permit
The weapon was a pistol or loaded firearm
notes: South Dakota enacted constitutional carry in 2019, allowing permit-less concealed carry for persons 18+ who are not prohibited. This statute primarily applies to prohibited persons or minors.

statute_title: Possession of Firearm by Convicted Felon
elements: Defendant possessed or had control of a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a crime of violence or a felony
Less than 15 years had elapsed since the conviction or release from imprisonment
notes: Persons convicted of crimes of violence lose firearm rights for 15 years after conviction or release. Certain felonies result in permanent prohibition.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Weapon — Violation of Restrictions
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In violation of location restrictions or other conditions
notes: Weapons are prohibited in certain locations including courthouses and schools regardless of permit status.

elements: Defendant discharged a firearm
In a reckless manner
Creating a risk of harm to persons or property
notes: Enhanced if injury results. May be charged alongside aggravated assault if directed at a person.

offense_class: Class 6 Felony (under $1,000); Class 5 Felony ($1,000-$2,500); Class 4 Felony ($2,500+)
penalty_max: 2 years to 10 years depending on loss amount
elements: Defendant used or attempted to use the personal identifying information of another
Without authorization
To obtain credit, money, goods, services, or other thing of value
notes: Includes using another's Social Security number, driver's license, financial account numbers, or other identifying information.

elements: Defendant was entrusted with property or funds
Defendant fraudulently converted the property to their own use
Without authorization
notes: Embezzlement is consolidated under the general theft statute in South Dakota. Classification based on value of property taken.

elements: Defendant falsely made, altered, forged, or counterfeited a written instrument
With intent to defraud
The instrument purported to be genuine
notes: Includes forging checks, legal documents, identification, and financial instruments.

elements: Defendant made, forged, or counterfeited any instrument
With intent to defraud another
The instrument was designed to appear genuine
notes: Counterfeiting is prosecuted under the forgery statute. Federal charges may also apply for counterfeiting U.S. currency.

statute_title: Making or Issuing a No-Account or Insufficient-Funds Check
offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (under $500); Class 1 Misdemeanor ($500-$1,000); Class 6 Felony ($1,000+)
penalty_max: 30 days to 2 years depending on amount
elements: Defendant issued a check or draft
Knowing at the time that there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Presumption of intent if check is not made good within 30 days of notice.

elements: Defendant knowingly presented false information in an insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
The claim was material
notes: Includes auto, health, life, and property insurance fraud.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of Credit or Debit Card
elements: Defendant used a credit or debit card
Knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, or revoked
With intent to defraud
notes: Penalties mirror the general theft statute based on the amount obtained.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (under $5,000); Class 4 Felony ($5,000-$100,000); Class 3 Felony ($100,000+)
penalty_max: 5 years to 15 years depending on amount
elements: Defendant conducted a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved was derived from unlawful activity
With intent to promote the unlawful activity or conceal the source
enhancements: Amount of laundered funds determines classification
notes: Also may be prosecuted federally under 18 U.S.C. § 1956.

elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
Defendant created a false impression of fact or value
With intent to defraud
notes: General fraud is prosecuted as theft by deception under the unified theft statute.

offense_class: Class C Felony (first degree); Class 1 Felony (if victim under 13)
elements: Defendant engaged in an act of sexual penetration with another person
Through force, coercion, or threats of bodily harm
Or the victim was incapable of giving consent
enhancements: Victim under 13 (Class 1 Felony, mandatory minimum 15 years)
notes: South Dakota uses 'rape' rather than 'sexual assault.' First-degree rape is a Class C Felony carrying up to life. Second-degree rape (SDCL § 22-22-1(1)) is a Class 1 Felony with mandatory minimums for child victims.

elements: Defendant engaged in an act of sexual penetration with another person
Through the use of force, coercion, or threats
Or the victim was incapable of giving consent due to physical or mental incapacity
enhancements: Victim under age 13 (Class 1 Felony, mandatory minimum 15 years)
notes: South Dakota classifies sexual assault as 'rape.' Rape of a child under 13 carries a mandatory 15-year minimum.

elements: Defendant exposed their genitals or intimate parts
In a public place or in view of the public
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
notes: Second or subsequent offense elevates to a Class 6 Felony. May trigger sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant engaged in or offered to engage in sexual activity
For a fee or anything of value
notes: Both the person soliciting and the person providing services may be charged. Promoting prostitution is a separate, more serious offense.

statute_title: Possession, Manufacture, or Distribution of Child Pornography
elements: Defendant possessed, manufactured, or distributed material depicting a minor in sexually explicit conduct
Defendant knew or should have known the material depicted a minor
notes: Federal charges commonly also apply. Sex offender registration required upon conviction.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, update, or verify registration information
notes: Registration requirements under SDCL Chapter 22-24B. Tier-based system with registration periods of 10 years, 25 years, or life.

statute_title: Rape — Victim Under Age of Consent
offense_class: Class 3 Felony (victim 13-15, defendant 3+ years older); Class 1 Felony (victim under 13)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with a victim
The victim was under the age of consent (16)
The defendant was older than the victim by 3 or more years
notes: Age of consent in South Dakota is 16. Three-year age gap provision for victims 13-15. Sexual contact with a child under 16 is prosecuted under SDCL § 22-22-7.

elements: Defendant intentionally caused public alarm, nuisance, or disturbance
By engaging in fighting, violent, or tumultuous behavior
Or making unreasonable noise or offensive utterances
notes: Common charge in public disturbance situations. May be combined with other charges.

elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a law enforcement officer
From effecting a lawful arrest
By using force or physical interference
notes: Applies even if the underlying arrest is later determined to be unlawful. Passive resistance alone is not typically sufficient.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor; Class 6 Felony if involving a felony investigation
elements: Defendant willfully obstructed, resisted, or opposed the administration of justice
Or interfered with a law enforcement officer in the performance of official duties
notes: Includes providing false information, hiding evidence, or interfering with an investigation.

offense_class: Punishable by fine and/or imprisonment at the court's discretion
penalty_max: 30 days (direct contempt); varies for indirect contempt
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or engaged in disorderly or disrespectful conduct in the court's presence
Or interfered with the orderly proceedings of the court
notes: Direct contempt (in the court's presence) may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing.

elements: Defendant appeared in a public place while intoxicated
To the degree that the defendant was a danger to themselves or others
Or was causing a public disturbance
notes: Protective custody may be used as an alternative to arrest.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (misdemeanor underlying); Class 6 Felony (felony underlying)
elements: Defendant was released on bond or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court at a specified time
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
enhancements: Underlying charge is a felony (Class 6 Felony)
notes: Bond may be forfeited and a bench warrant issued. Classification depends on the underlying charge.

statute_title: Filing False Report with Law Enforcement
elements: Defendant knowingly filed a false report
With a law enforcement agency
Claiming that a crime had been committed
notes: Defendant may also be liable for the costs of any investigation initiated based on the false report.

statute_title: Threatening to Commit a Crime of Violence
elements: Defendant threatened to commit a crime of violence
The threat was communicated to the victim or a third party
With intent to place the victim in fear of imminent serious bodily harm
notes: Terroristic threats are taken seriously and may be charged alongside aggravated assault.

elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath or affirmation
In a judicial proceeding or other proceeding where an oath is required
The statement was material to the proceeding
Defendant knew the statement was false
notes: Includes testimony in court, depositions, and sworn affidavits.

elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised anything of value
To a public official
With intent to influence the official's vote, decision, or action
notes: Both the person offering and the official accepting may be charged. Includes legislative, judicial, and executive officials.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (felony custody); Class 1 Misdemeanor (misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant was in lawful custody or confinement
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody
notes: Sentence for escape is consecutive to any sentence being served. Includes escape from prison, jail, or lawful custody of an officer.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first); Class 6 Felony (second or subsequent)
elements: Defendant intentionally, willfully, or maliciously treated an animal cruelly
Including torture, mutilation, or unnecessary suffering
notes: Second offense within the lifetime of the defendant is a Class 6 Felony.

penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
fine_max: Up to the maximum fine for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
The violation was willful and substantial
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose the original sentence. Hearing required before revocation.

elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Board of Pardons and Paroles makes revocation decisions. Defendant may be returned to serve the remainder of the original sentence.

statute_title: Aiding, Abetting, or Advising — Principal Liability
elements: A crime was committed by another person
Defendant knowingly aided, abetted, or advised the commission of the crime
Defendant intended to promote or facilitate the commission of the crime
notes: All persons who aid, abet, or advise the commission of a crime are equally liable as the principal.

offense_class: One class below the target offense (except Class A/B/C Felony attempts remain at the same class)
penalty_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific offense
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward commission
The conduct was strongly corroborative of the criminal intent
notes: Attempt is generally one class below the completed offense. Exception: attempt to commit a Class A, B, or C Felony remains at the same class.

elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
Defendant intended that the crime be committed
notes: Requires an overt act. Each conspirator may be liable for the acts of co-conspirators in furtherance of the conspiracy.
